title: Warrican's Six-Wicket Haul Not Enough as Pakistan Level West Indies Series
excerpt: Abdullah Shafique's unbeaten 160 and Sajid Khan's eight wickets power Pakistan to an eight-wicket win in Port of Spain, drawing the series 1-1.
body:
• Pakistan beat West Indies by eight wickets in the 2nd Test at Queen's Park Oval to level the series 1-1.
  • Jomel Warrican took 6/112 in Pakistan's first innings across 46 overs of sustained toil but received little batting support.
  • Abdullah Shafique scored an unbeaten 160, the first Pakistan batter to make 150+ in a West Indies Test since 1977.
  • The result has implications for the World Test Championship standings, with India's campaign also affected by how these teams perform.

Jomel Warrican bowled 46 overs and claimed six wickets, but Pakistan's batting depth proved too much for West Indies as the visitors secured an eight-wicket victory in the 2nd Test at Queen's Park Oval, Port of Spain, on August 6.

The result leveled the two-match series at 1-1 and ended Pakistan's eight-match losing streak away from home. Their last away Test win had come against Sri Lanka in July 2023.

Shafique's Masterclass

Abdullah Shafique anchored Pakistan's first innings with an unbeaten 160 off 323 balls, becoming the first Pakistan batter since 1977 to score more than 150 in a Test innings in the West Indies. His marathon knock helped Pakistan post 387, securing a crucial 43-run first-innings lead after West Indies had made 344.

"This comeback match felt like a debut for me," Shafique said. "I had been working hard for the last one year and was waiting for my opportunity. It came at an unexpected time but I grabbed it with both hands."

"You are always satisfied when you win. The most important thing was that we executed our plans whether it was how Abdullah Shafique batted in the first innings or how the spinners bowled in the second."

— Babar Azam, Pakistan captain

Warrican's Toil Goes Unrewarded

Warrican, who has emerged as one of Test cricket's most improved spinners in 2026, delivered another marathon spell. His 6/112 across 46 overs in Pakistan's first innings was built on relentless accuracy, keeping Pakistan's batters honest even as the pitch offered limited turn.

The left-arm spinner had been instrumental in West Indies' 90-run first-Test victory at Tarouba, where he took match-defining wickets. But the batting unit let him down in Port of Spain — West Indies crumbled for 117 in the second innings as Sajid Khan (4/32) and debutant Ali Usman combined to break the spine of the home side's batting.

WTC Implications

The series result carries significance for the World Test Championship standings. With India scheduled to play West Indies in Tests later this cycle, the form of both Caribbean and Pakistani players matters to Indian cricket fans tracking the WTC race.

Warrican's performances against Pakistan — and his earlier exploits in West Indies' historic win in Pakistan in January — mark him as a bowler India's batters will need to watch closely. He has already shown he can trouble the best, having dismissed Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul, and Shubman Gill in recent India-West Indies encounters.

What's Next

Pakistan next travel to England for a three-Test series beginning in Leeds on August 19. West Indies will look to regroup after squandering the momentum from their first-Test victory. Babar Azam sealed the win in the second innings with consecutive sixes off Warrican, an emphatic statement from a captain whose own form has been scrutinized.

Each of the last three Test series between Pakistan and West Indies have ended 1-1, underscoring the competitive balance between these two sides — even as both search for consistency in the longer format.
